objects.description: A place a tracked thing can be — a warehouse bin, a household room, a pasture. Nested to unbounded depth through parent_location_id; nothing constrains what kind may nest under what.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers. Server-minted; a caller-supplied id is never honoured.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stable human-readable identifier assigned once at creation, e.g. "L-1". Unlike name it never changes on update, so it is the one an operator can write on a label.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Short human-readable label, e.g. "Bin 12" or "Pantry shelf".

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Open-ended and descriptive only — "warehouse", "aisle", "bin", "room", "shelf", "pasture". Nothing enforces a vocabulary here, because every domain has its own.

fields.name: parent_location_id
fields.description: The enclosing location. Empty for a root location, which is how a tree is told from a forest.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of creation.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last update.

fields.name: deleted
fields.description: Soft-delete marker. Every read that lists rather than naming one row by id filters it out.

indexes.name: parent
indexes.description: Walks the tree: lists one location's direct children, which the descendant walk repeats per level.

objects.description: A trackable thing — either one physical unit, identified by its own tag, or a type tracked as a quantity. Which of the two it is is fixed at creation, because every movement already recorded against it means something different under the other reading.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers. Server-minted; a caller-supplied id is never honoured.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stable human-readable identifier assigned once at creation, e.g. "A-1". Unlike name it never changes on update.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Short human-readable label, e.g. "T-shirt, size M" or "Bessie".

fields.name: tracking_mode
fields.description: How this row's on-hand amount is read. "serialized" means the row is one physical unit, so its balance anywhere is 0 or 1; "fungible" means the row is a type and its quantity at a place is folded from the ledger. Immutable after creation.

fields.name: serial_tag
fields.description: The unique tag or serial carried by a serialized thing — an ear tag, an equipment serial. Empty for a fungible one, which is why its uniqueness index has to exclude the empty value.

fields.name: category
fields.description: Free-form grouping label, e.g. "livestock", "grocery", "electronics". Not constrained to a vocabulary.

fields.name: attributes_json
fields.description: A JSON-encoded object of whatever else this domain records about the thing — breed, warranty expiry, barcode. Stored as text rather than as a document column on purpose; promoting it is its own decision, not a side effect of a storage change.

fields.name: location_id
fields.description: Where the thing was last seen, maintained by the ledger rather than by a caller. A convenience only: the real balance at any place always comes from folding movements, never from this.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of creation.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last update.

fields.name: deleted
fields.description: Soft-delete marker. Every read that lists rather than naming one row by id filters it out.

indexes.name: serial_tag
indexes.description: Stops two live things claiming the same tag. Narrowed to non-empty tags because every fungible row leaves it blank, and blank is a value like any other to a unique index.

indexes.name: location
indexes.description: Lists what was last seen at one place.

objects.description: One append-only ledger entry. The balance at any thing-and-place pair is the fold of every entry affecting it, never a stored running total, so a correction is a new entry mirroring an old one rather than an edit to it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers. Server-minted; a caller-supplied id is never honoured.

fields.name: asset_id
fields.description: The thing this entry moves.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: What sort of entry this is. "arrived" enters from outside and names no origin; "transferred" moves between two places; "departed" leaves and names no destination; "adjusted" is a counted correction with no physical move, and the only kind whose quantity may be negative; "reversed" mirrors a prior entry.

fields.name: quantity
fields.description: How much this entry applies. Positive for every kind but "adjusted", which may be negative for a downward correction. Direction is otherwise carried by which of the two places is named, not by the sign.

fields.name: from_location_id
fields.description: Where this entry originated. Empty when the thing arrived from outside.

fields.name: to_location_id
fields.description: Where this entry ends up. Empty when the thing departed.

fields.name: performed_by
fields.description: Who recorded this entry, as an id this module never interprets. Required because an unattributed ledger entry is the gap a ledger exists to close.

fields.name: reverses_movement_id
fields.description: The entry this one mirrors, for kind "reversed". Empty otherwise. The mirrored entry is never edited or deleted.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Free-form reason, e.g. what a count variance turned out to be.

fields.name: occurred_at
fields.description: When the move actually happened, which differs from created_at for an entry queued offline and posted on reconnect.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the entry was posted.

indexes.name: asset
indexes.description: Folds one thing's ledger, which every balance read does.

indexes.name: reverses
indexes.description: Answers whether an entry has already been mirrored, which is what makes a reversal at-most-once.

objects.description: A reservation against a thing — quantity set aside before it actually moves, for a checkout or an order pick. Expires on its own if never committed, and supports committing less than was held, with the remainder given back.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers. Server-minted; a caller-supplied id is never honoured.

fields.name: asset_id
fields.description: The thing this reservation is against.

fields.name: location_id
fields.description: Where the quantity is reserved. Required, because what is available is only ever meaningful against one place.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Where the reservation is in its life. It starts "reserved" and every move out of that is terminal: fully "committed", "released" with nothing taken, or "partially_committed" with the remainder given back.

fields.name: quantity
fields.description: How much was originally set aside.

fields.name: committed_quantity
fields.description: How much of that was actually taken. Never more than quantity.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: When an uncommitted reservation is released without anyone asking. Read by the watchdog sweep.

fields.name: placed_by
fields.description: Who placed the reservation, as an id this module never interprets. Required for the same reason a ledger entry names who recorded it.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of creation.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last update.

indexes.name: asset
indexes.description: Finds the open reservations against one thing, which both the availability sum and the delete refusal need.

indexes.name: location
indexes.description: Finds the reservations at one place.

indexes.name: expiry
indexes.description: The watchdog's sweep for reservations past their time.

objects.description: The counter behind each kind of row's stable human-readable code. One row per kind of thing being numbered, holding the number to mint next.

fields.name: entity_type
fields.description: Which kind of row this counter numbers, as the module's own role word.

fields.name: next_number
fields.description: The number the next minted code will carry.
